description: Evidence tier per endpoint, derived from reports/results/baselines.csv by scripts/derive_evidence_tiers.py. Only 'validated' endpoints are presented as predictions and only they enter the composite score.

cns_toxicity.reason: trained on 3338 sequences from 2 independent assays and validated by training on one and testing on the other, with no shared sequences (ROC-AUC 0.78-0.83, CI low 0.76). It does not improve on the published G-count rule, which scores the same or better, so treat it as that rule rather than a new finding.

hepatocellular_injury.reason: the model's 95% CI reaches 0.29, below the best simple baseline (0.43), so it is not distinguishable from one crude sequence number Its probabilities are not calibrated: Brier skill -0.0307 against the base rate, below the 0.02 needed to be worth reading as a percentage, so treat the score as a ranking. On an independent screen of 149 LNA gapmers it ranks the 5 hepatotoxic ones no better than chance (ROC-AUC 0.31, CI 0.12-0.47). Too few positives to be conclusive, but there is no evidence this endpoint transfers off its own source.
